description: 45 cyber security logos explained by a brand designer, from CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Cloudflare to Wiz, 1Password, NordVPN, and the newest security startups.
intro:
A cyber security logo has to make people feel safe in a few seconds, so the best ones are strong enough to signal protection and distinctive enough not to look like every other shield and lock.

What makes a good cyber security logo?

Protection without cliches: shields, locks, and keys are everywhere in security, so the strongest brands find their own symbol, like the CrowdStrike falcon, the Fortinet firewall O, or the Arctic Wolf hidden in a mountain.

Confidence: heavy, wide, or italic type, like Rapid7, Palo Alto Networks, and Wiz, makes a security company feel fast and capable.

Color with purpose: most security brands use black, navy, and blue, which is exactly why orange, purple, and red logos, like Cloudflare, SentinelOne, and ExpressVPN, stand out.

Below are 45 cyber security logos in five groups, from industry leaders and cloud security to new startups, consumer privacy brands, and security startups to watch. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation.

logoResearch.name: CrowdStrike
logoResearch.verifiedFact: CrowdStrike is a US cybersecurity company known for its Falcon endpoint protection platform.
observations: A falcon's claw marks slash through the C, an aggressive symbol for a company that hunts attackers.
Heavy, wide capitals make the name feel strong and military.

logoResearch.name: Palo Alto Networks
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Palo Alto Networks is one of the largest cybersecurity companies, known for its firewalls and security platforms.
observations: Stacked orange slashes form a dynamic symbol, like a firewall of parallel layers.
A heavy lowercase paloalto with a tiny NETWORKS line keeps the long name compact.

logoResearch.name: Fortinet
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Fortinet is a US cybersecurity company known for its FortiGate firewalls.
observations: The O is replaced by a red grid, like a fortress wall or a firewall.
Wide, squared capitals feel engineered and solid.

logoResearch.name: Zscaler
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zscaler is a cloud security company focused on zero trust access.
observations: A blue cloud with a speed line shows security delivered from the cloud.
An italic, bold wordmark adds speed and momentum.

logoResearch.name: Check Point
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Check Point Software is an Israeli-American cybersecurity company and an early pioneer of the firewall.
observations: A pink-red symbol with a dot looks like a checkpoint marker or a shield in motion.
The stacked layout puts the symbol above bold, black capitals.

logoResearch.name: Cloudflare
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Cloudflare is a connectivity and security cloud that protects millions of websites.
observations: An orange cloud, the most literal symbol for a cloud company, is instantly recognizable.
Wide, spaced capitals under the cloud make the brand feel stable.

logoResearch.name: Okta
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Okta is an identity and access management company.
observations: A sunburst made of short rays surrounds an empty center, like a lens or a sun.
A light, rounded lowercase wordmark keeps an identity company friendly.

logoResearch.name: SentinelOne
logoResearch.verifiedFact: SentinelOne is an AI-powered endpoint and cloud security company.
observations: Purple vertical bars form a stylized S, like a sentinel's shield or a signal.
Purple stands out in a category full of blue, black, and red.

logoResearch.name: Proofpoint

observations: A heavy, rounded lowercase wordmark with no symbol.
A small period at the end makes the name feel like a confident statement.

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 cyber security logos in one consistent format, grouped into security leaders, cloud and identity, new startups, consumer and privacy, and security startups to watch.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for how good the security product is.
sectionIntroductions: The biggest security companies use bold, confident logos that look as strong as the protection they sell.
Cloud and identity security brands sell to developers and IT teams, so their logos are clean, technical, and modern.
Newer security startups are the most playful in the category, with mascots, gradients, and friendly lowercase type.
Consumer security and privacy brands sell to everyday people, so their logos are simpler, warmer, and easy to trust.
These younger security companies show how far a small brand can go with one clear symbol.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of cyber security logos, not a ranking of security products.
Look at how each logo signals protection and how much it relies on shields, locks, and other common symbols.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo signals protection without relying only on a generic shield.

findings.heading: The best security symbols avoid the obvious
findings.text: The CrowdStrike falcon, the Fortinet firewall O, and the Arctic Wolf hidden in a mountain are far more memorable than another padlock.

findings.heading: Animals are a security favorite
findings.text: Falcons, wolves, panthers, sharks, and even an octopus show up because predators and guardians signal protection.

findings.heading: Startups are getting friendlier
findings.text: Chainguard, Tines, Island, and Cyera use soft shapes and lowercase type, a clear break from the dark, aggressive look of older security brands.

findings.heading: Shields still work when they are simple
findings.text: Bitwarden, Securly, and Socket prove a shield can still feel fresh when it is flat, simple, and paired with one strong color.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new cyber security logo
checklistItems: Does it signal protection without relying on a generic shield or padlock?
Is the symbol simple enough to work as a favicon and an app icon?
Does it feel confident without looking aggressive or scary?

faq.question: What makes a good cyber security logo?
faq.answer: A good cyber security logo signals protection and confidence without relying on a generic shield or padlock. The strongest examples, like CrowdStrike, Fortinet, and Cloudflare, use one ownable symbol, bold type, and a color that stands out from the navy and black of most competitors.

faq.question: Should a cyber security logo use a shield or a lock?
faq.answer: It can, but shields and locks are so common in security that they rarely stand out. If you use one, keep it flat and simple and pair it with a strong color, like Bitwarden or Securly, or find your own metaphor, like an animal or a firewall.

faq.question: What colors are best for cyber security logos?
faq.answer: Blue, navy, and black dominate security because they feel stable and trustworthy. Brands that want to stand out often use orange, purple, or red instead, like Cloudflare, SentinelOne, and ExpressVPN.
